Hanna HI99121 with HI12923 soil electrode

This manual describes 10 g dry, 2 mm-sieved soil plus 25 mL HI7051 soil preparation solution, mixed 30 seconds and rested 5 minutes before immersion. It also describes a separate direct-soil method with a suitable probe. Neither is the 20 g plus 20 mL distilled-water source process card.

UC Davis documents separate 1:1 and 1:2 soil-to-deionized-water pH methods; method choice and liquid basis must accompany the result. This summary does not prescribe the source card's wait time or the HI99121 preparation solution.

The trainer records the actual meter, probe, manual revision, chosen preparation method, liquid, mass-to-volume ratio and basis, buffer set, calibration acceptance or check rules, electrode care, SDS where applicable, and waste route before a physical learner is scored. If unavailable, use online rehearsal only and mark practice unassessed.

sourceBindings.text: Check sample ID, PPE, actual probe and complete method
Gently break clods; use the specified 2 mm sieve
Weigh 20 g prepared soil for this card
Measure 20 mL distilled water for this card
Stir for 1 minute
Stand for 15 minutes; record real elapsed time
Accept the required buffer calibration
Place the suitable electrode without contact with grit or glass
Wait for an accepted stable display
Record actual value, identity and quality checks
Rinse between samples; clean and store by the probe manual

sourceBindings.text: Trainer sees each learner handle the labelled prepared soil, gently break clods without milling stones, sieve through 2 mm where required, weigh with a checked balance and measure the specified liquid in a clean graduated vessel; log actual mass, volume, liquid, ratio basis, stir and rest times for the declared method.
Pass only when every applicable stage follows the declared site protocol and source identity is preserved. A 20 g:20 mL source-card rehearsal alone does not pass a different actual method.

Record actual meter and probe, accepted calibration points and buffer lot/expiry, the device's acceptance indication or independent check, rinse/blot or care as its manual states, correct immersion/contact, and stable-reading condition; trainer observes each learner.
Pass only with accepted method-specific calibration and non-contaminating handling. A 'WRONG' buffer message, damaged/dry electrode or unstable reading stops scoring until corrected.

Three separate sample rows show actual pH, display resolution and method, operator, time and any recheck. Learner identifies when a reading is unstable, outside a check limit or inconsistent with sample preparation, then repeats only the affected stage under trainer direction.
Pass only when A, B and C are individually measured and recorded with defensible quality checks. Do not award a pass from a group sheet, a model key or three invented target numbers.

sourceBindings.text: The nine checks on this card are correct PPE, gentle clod crushing, 2 mm sieving, 20 g soil, 20 mL distilled water, one-minute stirring and 15-minute settling, manufacturer-directed buffer calibration, correct electrode placement, and recording a stable pH value. These quantities define the paper teaching scenario. Before physical use, the trainer verifies the actual meter and site method and matches the observable actions to that method without mixing procedures.
PPE selected for the actual site task
Crush aggregates gently without grinding stones
Collect 2 mm-sieved soil
Weigh 20 g in the source scenario
Measure 20 mL distilled water in the source scenario
Stir 1 minute and stand 15 minutes in the source scenario
Calibrate with accepted buffers per the actual manufacturer instructions
Place the correct probe correctly in the declared medium
Record final stable measured pH with sample and method identity
Record buffer identity, calibration acceptance and method separately from the original nine source rows.
Rinse between samples, record unstable or rejected runs and clean/store the electrode by its manual.
Trainer records each learner's own observed evidence and any correction; no automatic pass from a group mark.
